links.outcome: Classification accuracy, latency and span identification of fine-tuned discriminative vs generative LLMs
links.effect: Fine-tuned discriminative models consistently gave higher classification accuracy, lower inference latency, and more robust span-level identification than prompted or fine-tuned generative LLMs, given adequate training data.
links.quote: Our experiments demonstrate that fine-tuned discriminative models consistently provide higher classification accuracy, lower inference latency, and more robust span-level identification than either prompted or fine-tuned generative LLMs, given adequate training data.

links.outcome: Model performance differences across patient demographics and clinical departments
links.effect: Biases associated with patient demographics and clinical departments were reported as persistent challenges; no numbers given in abstract.
links.quote: Importantly, our results highlight persistent challenges, including difficulty extracting subtle sleep constructs such as sleep efficiency and daytime sleepiness, and biases associated with patient demographics and clinical departments.

unlisted_practices: Comparing prompted generative LLMs, fine-tuned generative LLMs and encoder-based classifiers for clinical note information extraction

screen.reason: The study benchmarks generative LLMs and discriminative NLP models for extracting multidimensional sleep health concepts from clinical notes across datasets (MIMIC-III and pediatric corpus), assessing performance and biases without testing a deployment safeguard or practice.
